name: Paper Cut
traits: layered cut shapes of coloured card stacked a few millimetres apart
exposed white or fibrous edges where the paper was cut or torn
small real cast shadows between layers
bestFor: simple product stories with clear shapes
suits: eco, garden, food, stationery and gift products; friendly, natural, handmade brands
stylePara: Layered paper-cut animation shot on a tabletop: every character, prop and background is cut from matte coloured card and tissue, stacked in four to six layers a few millimetres apart; edges show the white core of the card or a soft torn fibre; each layer casts a small soft shadow on the one behind it; surfaces show paper grain and slight warping; characters are flat cut-outs with jointed limbs held by tiny pins; light comes from one warm lamp at the side, so depth reads only through shadows and focus, like a miniature paper theatre.

rendering.line: no drawn outlines: shapes are defined by cut edges, with a thin white or fibre edge showing the paper core
rendering.shading: only real cast shadows between layers and a soft falloff across a slightly curled sheet; no painted shading
rendering.colour: flat matte card colours, one colour per piece, a few patterned papers; the product cut in its exact colours
rendering.texture: paper grain, cut and torn edges, tiny wrinkles, slight warping, tissue translucency where light passes
rendering.lighting: one warm side lamp plus soft fill; shallow depth of field across the layers

motion: Stop-motion cut-out animation on twos: pieces move in small stepped jumps, rotating on their pin joints; the layers slide past each other on fixed planes, never bending in 3D; held poses are completely still; mouths and eyes are swapped paper pieces.
camera: Front-on rostrum or tabletop camera, locked or on a slow slider; focus pulls between layers; push-ins stop short of the paper surface; no camera turning around the set, because the flat layers would show.
avoid: smooth vector shapes with digital gradients
paper texture swimming across moving pieces
printed letters on cut paper props
sheets: Each character is shown as its set of cut pieces laid flat (head, body, limbs, two mouth shapes) and assembled front and profile; the place is shown as its layer stack from the front and at a slight angle so the gaps read; the product is a cut-paper version in its exact colours, with the label as plain shapes.
risk: Seedance wants to give paper characters volume and turn them in 3D, and to let the paper grain slide across pieces as they move; repeat 'flat paper layers on fixed planes, rotate only on pin joints, stepped on twos' in MOTION and keep the camera frontal. Three-quarter turns are the weak spot: plan profile or front poses.

example.prompt: Layered paper-cut still on a tabletop set: a flat cut-out woman in her thirties with a dark paper bun and an orange card top, jointed with tiny pins, holds a small green tissue-and-card bottle with a yellow cap; a sunny kitchen built from four layers of matte coloured card with a warm side lamp casting small shadows between layers, a droopy fern of torn green paper on the windowsill; white cut edges, paper grain, shallow depth of field. Vertical 9:16. No text.
